research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12140 (44 FR 31159, Federal Register of May 31, 1979; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Delegation of Authorities Relating To Motor Gasoline End-User Allocation and signed May 29, 1979. The dossier’s automatic split (a lead fragment and fragments (a), (a)(1), (a)(2) and (c)) covered only part of section 1-102 and omitted sections 1-101, 1-103, 1-104 and 1-105 as units. The operative commands are the sections 1-101 to 1-104 and the two sentences of section 1-105 of the original; the page-break header and the date line are not commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12140, whose subject line describes delegating authorities relating to motor gasoline end-user allocation. The sunset sentence of section 1-105 was deleted by Executive Order 12162 (1979-09-28), which is the first end of that clause; the other clauses end on 1986-02-25. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. Executive Order 12287 of January 28, 1981 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12287.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) exempted all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls adopted under that Act without naming this order; it is likewise a disclosed candidate earlier end and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in the printings of EO 12162. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
